correctness.rationale: All subsets of a fixed ten-vertex Petersen graph are enumerated by two independently implemented face predicates; a complete reproducible matching pairs 258 of 260 nonempty faces in 129 disjoint Hasse pairs. The remaining masks 1 and 402 have dimensions 0 and 3. Explicit enumeration of all 860 directed Hasse arcs and full topological sorting proves acyclicity. Forman discrete Morse theory leaves a 0-cell and 3-cell with constant attaching map, hence S^3. The binary homology check is supplementary, not the basis of the integral homotopy conclusion.

originality.rationale: Material comparison with four full primary papers (arXiv:2605.25150, 2001.05448, 2505.06614, 2604.12606), several direct alias and statement searches, the published nearest scientific results and the existing same-topic claims found no homotopy theorem for the vertex-based two-independence complex of the Petersen graph. The closest Petersen records concern distinct edge-matching, Morse, or cut complexes; the chordal/tree results do not apply to a cubic girth-five graph. Unindexed/unpublished equivalents remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished identical computation cannot be ruled out.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed; reproducibility is by finite executable certificate and stated proof.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the canonical smallest cubic graph of girth five and an important benchmark outside the tree/chordal higher-independence theory. The natural, unmodified r=2 complex has dimension five yet nonpure facets; proving it has the exact integral homotopy type of a three-sphere provides a motivated natural homotopy invariant and structural counterpoint to purely combinatorial purity tests. A complete acyclic matching upgrades ranks to a genuine homotopy classification. No all-graph generalization or paper-sized consequence is asserted.
